rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: CHAP LXXII What manner of Death CANTERBURY should dye
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The chapter asks about the manner of death of the Archbishop of Canterbury.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Historical case, no independently frozen contemporary question.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: what manner of Death Canterbury should dye
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly frames a concern about how the already incarcerated Archbishop might be killed.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Archbishop identity and execution risk publicly known; not a secret event.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: original circular horoscope printed on page
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: An original round twelve-house figure accompanies the question.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Do not borrow a preceding spouse-case square chart.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The center of the original horoscope prints 3 December 1644.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Original 17th-century time/calendar standard not independently reconciled.

rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The center of the figure prints 2:24 PM.
rules.limits_and_attribution: No external prospective chart freeze or witness.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: hor astr Sun
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The center also records a planetary hour-ruler notation.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Do not infer a separate clock or location.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: none wisest men could better have represented person
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly claims the chart powerfully represented Laud and his situation.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Self-evaluated retrospectively; no blind comparison with decoys.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: old man in present state of trouble
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The text explicitly references an elderly churchman already involved in political strife.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Known confounder before astrological judgment; no novel risk identification.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: present state condition and manner of death
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The author considers current circumstances and later purported mode of execution.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Current imprisonment and prospective manner must not be scored as one success.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Churchman ascendant Capricorn cusp ninth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: For the cleric, Capricorn at the ninth-house cusp is used as his derived ascendant.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Not the radical first-house ascendant.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Saturn Lord of sign
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is used as Laud significator through Capricorn rulership.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Do not assign the bishop to the questioner default first lord.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Saturn in Aries his Fall
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is described in Aries in its fall.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Period dignity assertion not independently computed.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: a long time Retrograde
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is said to have been retrograde a long time.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Timing/ephemeris parity not independently performed.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Saturn in twelfth, fourth from his ascendant
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is placed in radical twelfth, derived fourth from the cleric ascendant.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Radical/derived house relation essential.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: violent spirit, turbulent, envious
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly describes the cleric in unfavorable character terms.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Historical opinion, not a verified psychology diagnosis.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: involved in troubles, imprisoned
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The source relates the chart to imprisonment and turmoil.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Already observable public history at December 1644.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Jupiter general significator Church-men
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Jupiter is invoked as general significator of clergy.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Separate from personal lord Saturn.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: eminency in Commonwealth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The source emphasizes the public prominence of the churchman.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Pre-existing historical status, no predictive novelty.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Jupiter Retrograde fixed Stars Mars and Moon nature
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The figure is linked to retrogradation and a class of fixed stars.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Which precise stars/longitudes have not been validated.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: deep laden with misfortunes and vulgar Clamours
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The source describes existing troubles and public condemnation.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Not a prospective forecast; contemporaneous context already known.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Moon Lady of fourth in Figure
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon is assigned to the radical fourth house.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Original sentence continues across the physical page boundary.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: but eighth as to his ascendant
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon also rules the eighth house derived from the ninth-house cleric ascendant.
rules.limits_and_attribution: The two roles must not be conflated.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Moon separates from Saturn
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly describes the Moon separating from Saturn.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Backward-looking separation, not identical to a future applying aspect.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Moon applies opposition Sun near eighth cusp
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon is said to apply by opposition to Sun near the eighth-house cusp.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Original aspect geometry and precise house referent require verification.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Sun in fiery Sign
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Sun is described as in a fire sign.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Elemental association is part of source logic, not a clinical mechanism.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Sun applies opposition Mars
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Sun is described as applying to an opposition of Mars.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Application direction and linked aspect distinct from Moon-Sun opposition.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Mars Dispositor of aged Bishop
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Mars is treated as dispositor of the bishop significator.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Explicit intermediary between Sun and represented person.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Mars in Ayery Sign and humane
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Mars is described in an airy and human sign.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Original classification untested; preserve literal source language.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: should not be hanged
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says he judged Laud would not be executed by hanging.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Prospective timing and independent forecast documentation absent.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: but suffer a more noble kind of death
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He predicts an alternative execution method termed more noble.
rules.limits_and_attribution: The printed forecast does not explicitly specify beheading by name.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: within space six or seven weeks or thereabouts
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The author gives a broad six/seven-week approximate period.
rules.limits_and_attribution: The qualifier or thereabouts is material; no exact Jan10 prediction.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: Moon wanted seven degrees of body Mars
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He says Moon lacked seven degrees to reach Mars, supplying the claimed interval.
rules.limits_and_attribution: This aspect relation and choice of weeks require ephemeris parity.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: beheaded about tenth January following
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says Laud was beheaded about 10 January following his December chart.
rules.limits_and_attribution: The historic 10 January 1645 execution is independently corroborated, but not Lilly forecast.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: 10 January 1645 Tower Hill
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The Bodleian biographical collection independently dates the beheading to 10 January 1645.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Historical event provenance only; does not authenticate a prospective horoscope prediction.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: December 3 to January 10 is shorter than six weeks
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The actual interval precedes the strict six-week lower bound, but author used or thereabouts.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Do not score as an exact six/seven-week hit without frozen tolerance.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: I write not as rejoiced death
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says he did not rejoice in the execution.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Personal authorial claim, not an observed astrological outcome.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: ever honoured man though never acquainted
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He says he respected Laud but never personally knew him.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Authorship stance rather than testimony from a direct personal witness.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: great uncertainty of humane affairs
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He expresses sorrow and calls human affairs uncertain.
rules.limits_and_attribution: This comment cannot be treated as scientific calibration of the forecast.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: liberal Maecenas to Oxford, good manuscripts
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The author praises Laud as benefactor to Oxford University and collector of manuscripts.
rules.limits_and_attribution: A historical biographical claim, not a predictive rule.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: let imperfections be buried in silence
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly urges charity in judging faults after death.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Not an astrological prediction.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: not a Martyr as one Else did
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He rejects a competing description of Laud as martyr.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Contested seventeenth-century political/religious framing.

rules.original_short_anchor_not_complete_quote: sentence of Parliament brought to his end
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The death is described as resulting from Parliament decision.
rules.limits_and_attribution: Historical context of already advanced proceedings, not a surprising unknown outcome.
